title: Scaling Hub: adjustable throughput targets, policy simulator, and immutable audit trail
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement:
Customers running Redwood Dedicated need a single place in Console to: 1) set and simulate throughput guarantees (per-fleet, per-model, per-route), 2) author autoscaling policies (min/max pool, cooldowns, schedule, buffer targets) with clear cost/latency tradeoffs, and 3) review an immutable change history with diffs for regulatory and on-call workflows. Current controls are fragmented across Fleet Settings, Deployment pages and an adhoc audit table; this causes confusion during incidents and when proving SLA compliance.

Goal:
Ship a cohesive "Scaling Hub" surface in Console that unifies scaling controls, a throughput dashboard with simulated impact, and an exportable, immutable change history including who changed what and why. The surface should support RBAC for operator roles, manual overrides with automatic rollback windows, and link directly to runtime metrics and cost estimates.

Scope (this ticket):
- Design and implement the Console UI for: adjustable throughput targets, a policy simulator (instant feedback on cost/latency), and a chronological change history with diff view and export.
- Hooks for backend APIs (policy apply, simulate, history export) will be consumed by engineering; backend implementation tracked in ENG-49810.
- MVP will cover per-fleet and per-model policies; per-route knobs are documented but deferred to follow-up.

Out of scope:
- Full RBAC enforcement (backend required) beyond UI gating and prompts.
- On-prem installation packaging.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Scaling Hub page added under Console > Capacity with header, breadcrumbs and contextual help link to docs/confluence.

2) Adjustable throughput target control: user can set target in requests/sec or tokens/sec and toggle between hard guarantee vs. target-with-fallback. UI validates ranges and shows estimated token cost per hour.

3) Policy editor: create/edit autoscaling policy with fields: min_instances, max_instances, target_utilization_pct, cooldown_seconds, schedule (cron-like), and a weight for burst buffer. Saving the policy shows a 2-step confirmation that surfaces estimated monthly cost delta.

4) Simulator panel: given historical 7-day traffic sample (pulls from runtime metrics), simulator projects latency percentile and cost for current, proposed, and recommended policies. Simulator renders a side-by-side chart and a short text recommendation.

5) Change history: every policy create/edit/delete is recorded as an immutable entry with timestamp, actor, old values, new values, reason text, and optional link to a support ticket. Entries support a compact diff view and CSV export.
6) Manual override: operators can trigger a temporary manual scaling (up or down) with optional auto-rollback after N minutes. Overrides appear in history and include a TTL countdown in UI.
7) UX: All flows validated in usability sessions (n=6 engineers/ops) with an average SUS > 75 and no major usability blockers remaining.
8) Unit/integration tests cover UI validation, simulator baseline, and change history rendering. E2E smoke path for save/simulate/history should pass in CI.
9) Documentation: console docs page and a short runbook for on-call linking to the change history and rollback steps are published.
10) Privacy/compliance: When enabled, change history export redacts API keys and secrets; documented behavior in the Security section of the PRD.
notes:
Design trade-offs and decisions so far:
- We chose to show both requests/sec and tokens/sec because some customers reason in token budgets and others in request volume. Backend will accept canonical tokens/sec but UI will convert.
- Simulator will run client-side diffs on sampled metric windows to avoid heavy backend compute for MVP; engineering will add a server-side compute path for large fleets in a follow-up (ENG-50122).
- Audit trail is append-only in the UI and will consume immutable events surfaced by the backend event store; if backend cannot provide diffs we will compute field diffs in the frontend for display.
- Cost estimates are intentionally conservative (rounded up) to avoid under-promising cost impact.

Open questions:
- Should schedule use a human-friendly recurring scheduler (weekly/daypart) or accept cron expressions? (UX leaning: friendly presets + advanced cron field).
- RBAC surface: which permission granularity is required for canary vs production fleets? Need input from Security and Sales for enterprise contracts.

progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff sync with Eng (Marcus, Priya, Daniel) and Design (Sofia). Agreed MVP surface and simulator approach.
2026-02-25: Design first-pass complete; shared with PM and Eng for feedback. Highlighted need to surface cost delta before confirmation.
2026-03-04: Engineering spike completed (ENG-49810) — backend hooks for audit events and policy apply exist but need pagination and diffs. Feeds are available via /api/v1/fleets/{id}/scaling-history.
2026-03-09: Usability testing with 6 ops/engineers. Key iteration: add TTL countdown to manual overrides and show per-minute cost burn when override requested.
2026-03-12: Design signoff on visual diff component; engineering started frontend work (PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5492).
